title: Reconstruction of an abelian etale sheaf at an affine inverse limit
statement: Let I be small and cofiltered, D:I→Sch have qcqs objects and affine transition maps, and let s exhibit X as its limit. For any abelian etale sheaf F, the counit cocone A_i=p_i^*p_i*F→F of [def-sc-affine-limit-sheaf-approximation] is a colimit cocone. Equivalently its canonical comparison colim_i A_i→F is an isomorphism. This applies to arbitrary abelian sheaves, including the zero sheaf; it requires no bounded exponent.

source.place: Proof step 1: Reconstruction of an abelian etale sheaf at an affine inverse limit

proof.text: By epimorphy of the approximation comparison, q:colim A→F is epi.

Check monomorphy at the algebraically closed residue-field geometric points, which detect equality of sheaf maps. Geometric stalk functors preserve filtered colimits, and the forgetful functor from abelian groups preserves these filtered colimits, so every germ in the source of P(q) has a stage representative t.

If P(q) kills that representative, the counit kills it. The eventual-vanishing theorem gives an arrow to a later stage where t is zero. The colimit relation shows that the original germ is zero. Thus P(q) is injective for every such point and q is mono.
The sheaf category is abelian; mono and epi imply iso. Transport the standard colimit universal property along q to the counit cocone.
